name: sidecar-toolbox-tools
description:
A SidecarToolbox's tools are reachable and dispatchable in a replayed bundle.

This is the only bronze scenario that exercises the SIDECAR route into the runner's tool set. A sidecar tool is an MCP tool by the time the model sees it — sidecartoolbox.Synthesize hands mcptool.Synthesize a synthetic MCPServer built from the CR's own tools allowlist, and at replay the same single fake MCP stub serves it — but it ARRIVES by a different path than an MCPServer CR does: through AgentSession.status.resolvedSidecarToolboxes, not through AgentClass.spec.mcpServers.

That difference is what the bundle pins, and it costs the driver two things nothing else needed: the SidecarToolbox CR has to be stamped Valid=True (the AgentClass controller refuses to go Valid while a sidecarToolboxes[].ref points at a toolbox that is not), and the runner's sidecar probe has to be redirected at the harness stub (the endpoint is derived at runtime from a pod IP and an operator-allocated port, so no {{MCP_URL}} sentinel can be written into a manifest). Drop either and this bundle hangs in WaitForAgentClassValid or fails dispatch; every other bundle stays green.

lastToolResultContains is the load-bearing assertion. agentReplyContains alone would pass on a scripted transcript whether the sidecar dispatched or returned nothing at all, which is this suite's oldest lesson — assert on the TOOL RESULT, not the reply.

toolOutputs carries `nodes` even though the transcript never calls it, and that is not padding: mcp.Synthesize returns an error when the allowlist names a tool the live server does not expose, and the stub builds its tools/list from OnTool registrations alone. Delete the `nodes` entry and synthesis of the whole toolbox fails, taking `pods` with it.
